decision_conditions: The proposed single storey rear extension, by reason of its size, siting and depth, would have an overbearing effect upon the adjoining property at no. 5 Robinson Close. The extension would result in creating a sense of enclosure that is detrimental to the amenities of neighbouring occupiers, particularly given the constrained nature of the garden and its existing enclosure by mature trees. The proposal istherefore contrary to Core Strategy Policy CP30 and Development Management Document Policies DMD8, DMD11 and DMD37.

The proposed single storey side and rear wraparound extension, by reason of its excessive footprint, would result in a substantial reduction of private amenity space, diminishing the quality and usability of the remaining garden area. While the existing space is largely paved, the loss of the garden is considered unacceptable and detrimental to the living conditions of the occupants. The proposal is therefore contrary to Core Strategy Policy CP30 and Development Management Document Policy DMD8 and DMD9.

Insufficient arboricultural evidence has been provided, in the form of Tree Survey, Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan BS 5837:2012 to demonstrate that there would be no undue harm caused to nearby off-site trees and wooded area within the immediate vicinity of the proposed works. The trees are prominent and offer high amenity value and potential for damage to these trees caused by the development is unjustifiable and would not be acceptable. The proposal would therefore be contrary to the advice contained within the NPPF (2024), policies G7 of the London Plan and DMD80 of the Development Management Document (2014).
description: Single storey side and rear wraparound extension.
